answer: At a craft exchange, agents inspect a crystal shipment packed in velvet beneath a willow tree. The buyer creates one signed order ID and deposits its fee before inspectors are chosen by lottery. Payment is tied to that ID, a sealed sample and two independent inspection reports, so opening more seller accounts cannot multiply the fee. An attacker needs additional real orders, deposits and samples to earn more. Buyers and inspectors may collude or reuse samples, so the exchange audits random orders and freezes bonds when seals disagree.
